Simulate basic population dynamics model

Source: R/sim_pop.R
sim_abundance.Rd

Simulates a basic age-structured population using recruitment (R), total mortality (Z), and initial abundance (N0) functions. Optionally, a growth function may be provided to simulate lengths given age and generate an abundance-at-length matrix.

sim_abundance(
  ages = 1:20,
  years = 1:20,
  Z = sim_Z(),
  R = sim_R(),
  N0 = sim_N0(),
  growth = sim_growth(),
  weight = sim_weight(),
  maturity = sim_maturity(),
  maturity_by = "length"
)

Arguments

ages

A non-empty, finite numeric vector of ages, ascending in steps of one.

years

A non-empty, finite numeric vector of years, ascending in steps of one.

Z

A function for generating a total mortality matrix, such as sim_Z().

R

A function for generating a recruitment vector (i.e., abundance at min(ages)), such as sim_R().

N0

A function for generating a starting abundance vector (i.e., abundance at min(years)), such as sim_N0().

growth

A closure, such as sim_vonB(), for simulating length given age. This is used both to generate an abundance-at-length matrix and later for length simulation in sim_survey().

weight

Function returning expected kilograms at length, such as sim_weight(). Default lengths are centimetres. Shared by all fisheries.

maturity

Function returning probabilities of maturity, such as sim_maturity() or sim_logistic().

maturity_by

Trait supplied to maturity: "length" or "age".

Value

A list with the following elements:

  • ages: Vector of ages used in the simulation

  • lengths: Vector of length groups (depends on growth function)

  • years: Vector of years used in the simulation

  • R: Vector of recruitment values

  • N0: Vector of starting abundance values

  • Z: Matrix of total mortality values

  • N: Matrix of abundance-at-age

  • N_at_length: Matrix of abundance-at-length

  • sim_length: Function for simulating lengths given ages

  • sim_weight, sim_maturity, maturity_by: Shared biological relationships

  • B, B_at_length: Expected biomass (kg), by age/year and length/year

  • S, S_at_length: Expected mature biomass (kg), by age/year and length/year

Details

Abundance is simulated using a standard population dynamics model. If a growth function such as sim_vonB() is provided, it is used to create a corresponding abundance-at-length matrix. The same growth function is retained for use in sim_survey() to simulate lengths from catch-at-age survey data.

Note: The ability to simulate distributions by length is not yet implemented.

Biomass integrates weight over the discrete length-age key. Mature biomass integrates weight times maturity, retaining their association. S represents all mature fish under one curve, without a female fraction, spawning-season adjustment, or recruitment feedback. These are expected annual snapshots, not the biomass of a particular integer length-stock realization used by a fishery. Spatial simulation and round_sim() refresh summaries when abundance changes.

To migrate an older distributed simulation without regenerating its trajectory, explicitly attach the relationships, then call round_sim(): sim$sim_weight <- sim_weight(); sim$sim_maturity <- sim_maturity(); sim$maturity_by <- "length"; sim <- round_sim(sim). This uses existing cell rounding; it does not resimulate N or Z. For an older abundance-only object, attach the components before sim_distribution(). Biological defaults are not silently assigned to old objects.

See also

vignette("fisheries", package = "SimSurvey") for shared biological truth, multiple fisheries with user-supplied allocations, independent surveys, and the model equations.

Examples

R_fun <- sim_R(log_mean = log(100000), log_sd = 0.1, random_walk = TRUE, plot = TRUE)
R_fun(years = 1:100)

#> $sim_length
#> function (age = NULL, length_age_key = FALSE) 
#> {
#>     pred_length <- Linf - (Linf - L0) * exp(-K * age)

#>         lak <- matrix(NA, ncol = length(pred_length), nrow = length(breaks) - 
#>             1, dimnames = list(length = group_lengths(breaks, 
#>             length_group)[-length(breaks)], age = age))
#>         for (i in seq_along(breaks)[-1]) {
#>             for (j in seq_along(pred_length)) {
#>                 lak[i - 1, j] <- stats::pnorm(log(breaks[i]),

#>                   1]), log(pred_length[j]), sd = log_sd)
#>             }
#>         }
#>         lak <- lak[rowSums(lak) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
#>         if (plot) 
#>             graphics::image(x = as.numeric(colnames(lak)), y = as.numeric(rownames(lak)), 
#>                 z = t(lak), xlab = "Age", ylab = "Length", main = "P(Length | Age)", 
#>                 col = viridis::viridis(100))
#>         return(lak)
#>     }
#>     else {

#>         if (plot)

#>         return(length)
#>     }
#> }
